candidate.answerReason: 2011 minutes equals one day, nine hours, and 31 minutes. Starting at midnight on January 1 gives January 2 at 9:31 AM, agreeing with choice D.

methods.label: Separate the elapsed time into units
methods.explanation:
The beginning of January \(1\) is midnight. One full day contains \(24\times60=1440\) minutes, leaving
\[
2011-1440=571\text{ minutes}.
\]
Since \(571=9\times60+31\), the remaining time is \(9\) hours and \(31\) minutes. One day after the starting time is midnight on January \(2\), so the requested time is January \(2\) at \(9{:}31\) AM, choice \(\text{D}\).
methods.levelReason: Converting minutes to hours and tracking the change of date at midnight are elementary time calculations appropriate for AMC 8.

candidate.annotationRationale: The targets are hour-minute conversion and interpreting a full 24 hours as the start of the next day. Quotient-and-remainder reasoning separates complete hours from leftover minutes.
